title: The origin of the New Year's resolution“
paragraphs: Happy New Year! For many in the UK, if the New Year means anything, it means starting with a clean slate and turning over a new leaf. And to do this, many of us make New Year's resolutions – a list of ways that we intend to improve ourselves in the year ahead. We reflect on our past transgressions and resolve not to do them again. Refraining from smoking is ever popular, as is a vow to take up more exercise or spend more time with family. But where does the idea of a New Year's resolution come from?

The answer might lie 4,000 years ago in ancient Babylonia, according to History.com. The Babylonians are believed to be the first to hold recorded celebrations for the New Year. The 12-day-long celebration, Akitu, allowed them not only to reaffirm their loyalty to the king, or crown a new one, but also to pledge to the gods to pay their debts and return borrowed objects. For their 'good behaviour', they believed the gods would bestow favour upon them for the year to come. If not, there would be divine consequences!

The Romans too had similar traditions. New Year's Day was a time when senators would swear they had upheld the laws and city leaders and soldiers would take an oath of loyalty to the emperor. Incidentally, the month of January, is named after the Roman god Janus. He is the god of beginnings, transitions and time, among other things and is depicted as having two faces – one looking to the past and the other facing forward to the future.

The Romans may be long gone, but their legacy lives on. Come the turn of the year, our eyes turn inwards. We look at self-improvement, review our past mistakes, confess our wrongdoings, seek atonement and try to sharpen up in general. Ultimately, much like the Babylonians and Romans, we seek to reaffirm the best parts of ourselves, while leaving the dross behind.

Whether you're looking at a quick behavioural tweak, or a huge personality overhaul, you're taking part in a tradition that goes back centuries. I wish you all the best sticking to your resolutions. Happy New Year!

vocabulary.term: clean slate [kliːn sleɪt] 重新开始；清白的记录
vocabulary.entry: clean slate [kliːn sleɪt] 重新开始；清白的记录
vocabulary.example: After moving to a new city, he wanted a clean slate and left his old mistakes behind.
vocabulary.translation: 搬到新城市后，他想重新开始，把过去的错误都抛在了脑后。

vocabulary.term: turn over a new leaf [tɜːn ˈəʊvə(r) ə njuː liːf] 改过自新；洗心革面
vocabulary.entry: turn over a new leaf [tɜːn ˈəʊvə(r) ə njuː liːf] 改过自新；洗心革面
vocabulary.example: Realizing his bad habits were harmful, he decided to turn over a new leaf and live a healthier life.
vocabulary.translation: 意识到自己的坏习惯有害无益，他决定改过自新，过上更健康的生活。

vocabulary.term: New Year's resolutions [njuː jɪəz ˌrezəˈluːʃnz] 新年决心（复数）
vocabulary.entry: New Year's resolutions [njuː jɪəz ˌrezəˈluːʃnz] 新年决心（复数）
vocabulary.example: Most people make New Year's resolutions, but few manage to keep them for a whole year.
vocabulary.translation: 大多数人都会立下新年决心，但很少有人能坚持一整年。

vocabulary.term: transgressions [trænzˈɡreʃnz] n. 过错；违规行为（复数）
vocabulary.entry: transgressions [trænzˈɡreʃnz] n. 过错；违规行为（复数）
vocabulary.example: The manager warned the employees that any further transgressions would result in dismissal.
vocabulary.translation: 经理警告员工，再有任何违规行为就会被解雇。

vocabulary.term: refrain from [rɪˈfreɪn frəm] 避免；克制不做
vocabulary.entry: refrain from [rɪˈfreɪn frəm] 避免；克制不做
vocabulary.example: It is wise to refrain from making hasty decisions when you are angry.
vocabulary.translation: 生气的时候克制自己，不做草率的决定是明智的。

vocabulary.term: vow [vaʊ] n. 誓言；誓约
vocabulary.entry: vow [vaʊ] n. 誓言；誓约
vocabulary.example: She made a vow to herself that she would learn a new language within a year.
vocabulary.translation: 她对自己发誓，要在一年内学会一门新语言。

vocabulary.term: Babylonia [ˌbæbɪˈləʊniə] n. 巴比伦（古代美索不达米亚王国）
vocabulary.entry: Babylonia [ˌbæbɪˈləʊniə] n. 巴比伦（古代美索不达米亚王国）
vocabulary.example: Babylonia was famous for the Hanging Gardens, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
vocabulary.translation: 巴比伦以空中花园而闻名，空中花园是古代世界七大奇迹之一。

vocabulary.term: reaffirm [ˌriːəˈfɜːm] v. 重申；再次确认
vocabulary.entry: reaffirm [ˌriːəˈfɜːm] v. 重申；再次确认
vocabulary.example: The two countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening trade cooperation.
vocabulary.translation: 两国重申了加强贸易合作的承诺。

vocabulary.term: pledge to [pledʒ tuː] 向……发誓；承诺
vocabulary.entry: pledge to [pledʒ tuː] 向……发誓；承诺
vocabulary.example: The government pledged to provide more funding for public education.
vocabulary.translation: 政府承诺为公共教育提供更多资金。

vocabulary.term: bestow [bɪˈstəʊ] v. 赐予；给予
vocabulary.entry: bestow [bɪˈstəʊ] v. 赐予；给予
vocabulary.example: The committee decided to bestow the award on the most outstanding student of the year.
vocabulary.translation: 委员会决定将奖项授予本年度最优秀的学生。

vocabulary.term: divine consequences [dɪˈvaɪn ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz] 神圣的后果；天谴（复数）
vocabulary.entry: divine consequences [dɪˈvaɪn ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz] 神圣的后果；天谴（复数）
vocabulary.example: In some ancient cultures, people believed that disrespecting elders would bring divine consequences.
vocabulary.translation: 在一些古代文化中，人们认为不尊重长辈会招致天谴。

vocabulary.term: legacy [ˈleɡəsi] n. 遗产；传统
vocabulary.entry: legacy [ˈleɡəsi] n. 遗产；传统
vocabulary.example: The famous writer's legacy includes not only novels but also a set of values that inspire readers.
vocabulary.translation: 这位著名作家的遗产不仅包括小说，还有一套激励读者的价值观。

vocabulary.term: inwards [ˈɪnwədz] adv. 向内；向内心
vocabulary.entry: inwards [ˈɪnwədz] adv. 向内；向内心
vocabulary.example: The yoga instructor told us to breathe inwards and focus on our breathing rhythm.
vocabulary.translation: 瑜伽教练让我们向内呼吸，专注于自己的呼吸节奏。

vocabulary.term: atonement [əˈtəʊnmənt] n. 赎罪；补偿
vocabulary.entry: atonement [əˈtəʊnmənt] n. 赎罪；补偿
vocabulary.example: The man devoted his later years to atonement for the mistakes he made in his youth.
vocabulary.translation: 这个人把晚年的时光都用来弥补年轻时犯下的过错。

vocabulary.term: dross [drɒs] n. 糟粕；渣滓
vocabulary.entry: dross [drɒs] n. 糟粕；渣滓
vocabulary.example: This book contains some useful advice, but you need to sift out the dross to find it.
vocabulary.translation: 这本书里有一些有用的建议，但你需要剔除糟粕才能找到。

vocabulary.term: tweak [twiːk] n. 细微调整
vocabulary.entry: tweak [twiːk] n. 细微调整
vocabulary.example: The designer made a small tweak to the logo to make it more eye-catching.
vocabulary.translation: 设计师对标志做了一点细微调整，让它更引人注目。

vocabulary.term: overhaul [ˈəʊvəhɔːl] n. 彻底改革；全面改进
vocabulary.entry: overhaul [ˈəʊvəhɔːl] n. 彻底改革；全面改进
vocabulary.example: The school system is in need of a major overhaul to adapt to modern educational needs.
vocabulary.translation: 学校体系需要进行一次全面改革，以适应现代教育的需求。

vocabulary.term: oath of loyalty [əʊθ ɒv ˈlɔɪəlti] 效忠誓言
vocabulary.entry: oath of loyalty [əʊθ ɒv ˈlɔɪəlti] 效忠誓言
vocabulary.example: Upon taking office, the new prime minister took an oath of loyalty to the country and its people.
vocabulary.translation: 新任首相就职时，宣誓效忠国家和人民。

vocabulary.term: depicted as [dɪˈpɪktɪd æz] 被描绘为；被描述为（depict的过去分词/被动形式）
vocabulary.entry: depicted as [dɪˈpɪktɪd æz] 被描绘为；被描述为（depict的过去分词/被动形式）
vocabulary.example: In many fairy tales, witches are depicted as evil and cruel characters.
vocabulary.translation: 在许多童话故事里，女巫被描绘成邪恶残忍的角色。

vocabulary.term: stick to resolutions [stɪk tuː ˌrezəˈluːʃnz] 坚持决心（resolutions为复数）
vocabulary.entry: stick to resolutions [stɪk tuː ˌrezəˈluːʃnz] 坚持决心（resolutions为复数）
vocabulary.example: Setting realistic goals is the key to sticking to resolutions.
vocabulary.translation: 制定切实可行的目标是坚持决心的关键。

sentences.english: Happy New Year!
sentences.chinese: 新年快乐！

sentences.english: For many in the UK, if the New Year means anything, it means starting with a clean slate and turning over a new leaf.
sentences.chinese: 对许多英国人来说，新年若有什么意义，那便是重新开始、改过自新。

sentences.english: And to do this, many of us make New Year's resolutions – a list of ways that we intend to improve ourselves in the year ahead.
sentences.chinese: 为此，我们许多人会制定新年决心——一份计划在来年提升自我的清单。

sentences.english: We reflect on our past transgressions and resolve not to do them again.
sentences.chinese: 我们反思过去的过错，决心不再重犯。

sentences.english: Refraining from smoking is ever popular, as is a vow to take up more exercise or spend more time with family.
sentences.chinese: 戒烟向来很受欢迎，发誓要更多地锻炼身体或花更多的时间陪伴家人也同样常见。

sentences.english: But where does the idea of a New Year's resolution come from?
sentences.chinese: 但新年决心的想法源自何处呢？

sentences.english: The answer might lie 4,000 years ago in ancient Babylonia, according to History.com.
sentences.chinese: 据History.com网站记载，答案或许能追溯到4000年前的古代巴比伦。

sentences.english: The Babylonians are believed to be the first to hold recorded celebrations for the New Year.
sentences.chinese: 人们认为巴比伦人是最早有记载庆祝新年的民族。

sentences.english: The 12-day-long celebration, Akitu, allowed them not only to reaffirm their loyalty to the king, or crown a new one, but also to pledge to the gods to pay their debts and return borrowed objects.
sentences.chinese: 这场长达12天的庆典名为“Akitu”，在庆典中，他们不仅会重申对国王的忠诚（或为新国王加冕），还会向诸神发誓偿还债务、归还借来的物品。

sentences.english: For their 'good behaviour', they believed the gods would bestow favour upon them for the year to come. If not, there would be divine consequences!
sentences.chinese: 他们相信，凭借这种“良好行为”，诸神会在来年赐福于他们；否则，将面临神的惩罚！

sentences.english: The Romans too had similar traditions.
sentences.chinese: 罗马人也有类似的传统。

sentences.english: New Year's Day was a time when senators would swear they had upheld the laws and city leaders and soldiers would take an oath of loyalty to the emperor.
sentences.chinese: 新年当天，参议员会宣誓维护法律，城市官员和士兵会宣誓效忠皇帝。

sentences.english: Incidentally, the month of January, is named after the Roman god Janus.
sentences.chinese: 顺便说一句，一月（January）以罗马神雅努斯（Janus）命名。

sentences.english: He is the god of beginnings, transitions and time, among other things and is depicted as having two faces – one looking to the past and the other facing forward to the future.
sentences.chinese: 雅努斯是开端、过渡和时间等等之神，被描绘为有两张脸——一张回望过去，另一张展望未来。

sentences.english: The Romans may be long gone, but their legacy lives on.
sentences.chinese: 罗马人早已消逝，但他们的传统留存至今。

sentences.english: Come the turn of the year, our eyes turn inwards. We look at self-improvement, review our past mistakes, confess our wrongdoings, seek atonement and try to sharpen up in general.
sentences.chinese: 岁末年初，我们开始向内审视：关注自我提升，回顾过往错误，坦陈过失，寻求赎罪，并努力全面改进。

sentences.english: Ultimately, much like the Babylonians and Romans, we seek to reaffirm the best parts of ourselves, while leaving the dross behind.
sentences.chinese: 最终，和巴比伦人、罗马人一样，我们试图肯定自身最美好的部分，同时摒弃糟粕。

sentences.english: Whether you're looking at a quick behavioural tweak, or a huge personality overhaul, you're taking part in a tradition that goes back centuries.
sentences.chinese: 无论你是想快速改善行为，还是彻底重塑性格，你都在参与一项可追溯数百年的传统。

sentences.english: I wish you all the best sticking to your resolutions.
sentences.chinese: 祝愿大家都能坚持自己的决心。

sentences.english: Happy New Year!
sentences.chinese: 新年快乐！
